title: VBR force increase vs prone rest for prone physiotherapy exercises (arm lift, arm + contralateral leg)
condition: in vivo, VBR + posterior fixator, physiotherapy exercises

quantity.name: increase of peak resultant force on VBR
quantity.definition: RELATIVE: peak resultant VBR force during the exercise minus the mean resultant force in the relaxed resting prone position (reference activity = relaxed prone rest). Per patient median and range over trials.

source.authors: Rohlmann A, Schwachmeyer V, Graichen F, Bergmann G
source.sample: 5 patients (4 M, 1 F) with telemeterised VBR (WP1-WP4 at L1, WP5 at L3); 3-5 patients per exercise; in vivo; A3 compression fracture; posterior internal fixator (2 segments in 3 patients, 4 segments in WP3 and WP4) + telemeterised VBR; measurements few days to 65 months post-op

protocol.summary: Physiotherapeutic exercises in the prone position (Table 1 descriptions), few general instructions, performed over ~5 years of follow-up.
how_to_simulate: Model the patient lying relaxed prone; record resting resultant force at the implant level (L1)
Simulate lifting one cranially stretched straight arm, and lifting one arm with the contralateral leg
Report peak resultant force minus resting value
A whole-spine MSK model outputs total segment compression at the implant level, not the implant share; compare trends/relative changes unless the model includes the VBR and posterior fixator

subject_model.implant_note: VBR replaces parts of the fractured vertebral body and the adjacent discs; posterior internal fixator remains in situ
subject_model.source: Rohlmann 2014c gives only group ranges (4 M/1 F, 62-71 y, 60-74 kg, 168-180 cm, BMI 19-26, L1 in WP1-WP4, L3 in WP5); per-patient values taken from the same WP1-WP5 cohort tables (Rohlmann 2014a Table 1 / Dreischarf 2015 Table 1)

protocol.notes: Load measured on a telemeterised vertebral body replacement (modified Synex, 6 load components, accuracy ~2% force / 5% moment of 3000 N / 20 Nm calibration range) that shares the load with the posterior internal fixator, residual vertebral bone and bone graft; the VBR force is NOT the total spinal load. Evaluation: peak resultant force during the exercise minus the mean resultant force in the relaxed resting position (same posture) = force increase. Per patient: median and range over trials; "Average" bar = median of the patient medians with range of the medians. Lying resultant VBR force was usually <50 N (up to 100 N with muscle tension). Only general instructions were given; trials span ~5 years post-op. Text: arm lift average increase ~185 N; arm + contralateral leg mostly smaller (~100 N). Data from WP1, WP2, WP4 only.
